The Ca/Si/Al/O stoichiometry governs ion mobility in glass through a percolation threshold where modifier cations form connected pathways; specifically, Ca concentration above 15 mol% triggers a sharp increase in conductivity due to the emergence of long-range Ca-O-Ca networks.

Oxygen vacancy clusters in Ca-Si-Al-O glasses act as low-energy migration channels for Ca²⁺ ions, reducing the activation energy for diffusion by >0.5 eV compared to pristine glass; this effect is maximized when vacancies are aligned along Si-O-Si bridges.

The local tetrahedral order parameter (Q⁴) in Ca-Si-Al-O glasses exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on Al₂O₃ content, peaking at ~10 mol% Al₂O₃ before declining due to network depolymerization; this correlates with a maximum in mechanical stability and a minimum in ion mobility.
